fields.value: Optically induced crossover from weak to strong coupling regime between surface plasmon polaritons and photochromic molecules

dsDescriptionValue.value: We demonstrate optically induced crossover from weak to strong coupling regime in a single photonic system consisting of propagating surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) on a planar silver film and UV-switchable photochromic molecules. A gradual increase of the vacuum Rabi splitting upon increasing UV exposure is observed, as well as intriguing behavior, where the reflectivity initially decreases due to increased losses at the weak coupling regime, and then increases due to the emergence of the strongly coupled modes and the associated band gap formation at the resonance frequency of the uncoupled states. This work explicitly demonstrates optical tunability of the degree of hybridization of the SPP and exciton modes, spanning the range from weak to intermediate and finally to strong coupling regime.
